clue.text: Hiding obsession about skin eruption

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for obsession wraps the skin eruption

parts.note: a thing, as in 'he has a thing about trains', is an obsession
a rash is an outbreak on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone fixated on a spot on their skin is hiding away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' looks like concealment but is the noun for a beating; 'about' wraps the obsession round the eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a severe beating, the same punishment as a thrashing.

clue.text: Apparatus for jumpers and stockings with a run in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle says the run sits at the centre of the stockings

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Laddered stockings, as if snagged on gym equipment by jumpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' puts R inside HOSE. 'jumpers' looks like knitwear but means gymnasts who vault.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulting horse is a padded gym apparatus that gymnasts leap over.

clue.text: To stimulate leaders of any riot, one usually starts early

indicators.note: leaders of asks for the opening letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: An agitator who stirs up riots tends to start the trouble early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' picks the first letter of each of the six words any, riot, one, usually, starts, early.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse something is to excite or provoke it into activity.

clue.text: Number in seraglio in this part of New York?

indicators.note: in places the number within the word for the seraglio

parts.note: a seraglio is a harem, the women's quarters of a palace
L is the Roman numeral fifty, so a number

explanation.surface: A question about how many women live in a harem in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L, the Roman fifty, inside HAREM.
explanation.definitionFit: This district of upper Manhattan is a famous neighbourhood of the city.

clue.text: Unpleasant short name to stay around

parts.note: N is a standard short form of name

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the word stay are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty character with a short name who hangs about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is a loose anagram signal here: the four letters of 'stay' are rearranged after the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant is disagreeable or offensive, just like something horrid.

clue.text: Ancient monument lending weight to social status

parts.note: standing is one's position or status in society
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A monument that adds gravitas to someone's place in society.
explanation.walkthrough: STONE is a British unit of body weight equal to 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalith set upright in prehistoric times, such as those at Stonehenge, is a classic ancient monument.

clue.text: The professor's hypothesis?

parts.note: a learned academic's theory would literally be a learned person's surmise, playing on the phrase for an informed estimate

explanation.definitionFit: An informed estimate based on knowledge is literally what a schooled academic would propose as a hypothesis.

clue.text: Right at sea radar does bits, going around

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters spin into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A ship's radar picks out fragments while circling at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' signals an anagram of RADAR DOES BITS.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the right-hand side when facing forward is the nautical term for right.

clue.text: It provides rounds for serving soldiers

definitions.text: It provides rounds for serving soldiers

parts.words: It provides rounds for serving soldiers
parts.note: reads like army supply of ammunition, but rounds are slices of bread and soldiers are strips of toast served at breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, soldiers are fingers of toast dipped in boiled eggs, and a round is a slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: This breakfast-table holder keeps rounds of toast upright, the strips of which British children call soldiers.

clue.text: Stiffly slanted in wily grip

indicators.note: in, with the wily one's grip, places the slanted piece inside the crafty word

parts.note: sly means crafty or wily
tilted means slanted or leaning

explanation.surface: Something held awkwardly at an angle in a cunning grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'grip' only pictures the crafty word holding the slanted one.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking stiltedly means in a stiff, formal and unnatural manner.

clue.text: No heavy cat!

definitions.meaning: a weight of only about 28 grams is far from heavy
the snow leopard of Central Asia is also known by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The small unit of weight is hardly heavy, and the same word names the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Vessel originally Dutch yet starts with eight from Germany

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letter of the word yet

parts.note: acht is German for eight

explanation.surface: A vessel of Dutch origin with an eight-strong German crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition notes the word comes from Dutch jacht; 'starts' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleasure boat takes its name from a Dutch word for a fast hunting ship.

clue.text: Stipulation for limited periods

definitions.meaning: the conditions of an agreement; the plural answer stands for a singular stipulation
school or court sessions of fixed length

explanation.definitionFit: Conditions laid down in a contract are its stipulations, and fixed academic sessions are also called by this word.

clue.text: Peculator trapped by his own kind?

definitions.text: Peculator trapped by his own kind?

parts.words: Peculator trapped by his own kind?
parts.note: alludes to the saying that it takes a crook to catch a crook

explanation.definitionFit: A peculator is an embezzler, one who steals, and the proverb says one is best caught by another of the same trade.

clue.text: See the scoundrel go back in the French way

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the French word for a street

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way

indicators.note: back means the word go is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch the villain retreat in a Gallic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See the' is padding that makes the surface read; 'back' turns 'go' and 'in' places it inside the French street.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest rascal, much like a villain.

clue.text: Dropped off 'spelt incorrectly

indicators.note: incorrectly suggests the letters of the word are in the wrong order and must be fixed

explanation.surface: A complaint that a word was misspelt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrectly' signals an anagram of SPELT.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep, so dropped off means had a nap.

clue.text: Second enchantress to change course

parts.note: a witch is a female sorcerer or enchantress

explanation.surface: A second sorceress decides to alter her path.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap direction or change from one thing to another.

clue.text: Pulse showing fast time — 1.50?

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral one and L is fifty

explanation.surface: A pulse rate or racing time shown as one minute fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.50' is read as I and L, the Roman one and fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is an edible seed such as a bean, pea or this small lens-shaped legume.

clue.text: Score of one not opening in fireplace

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: in cricket a single is a run scoring one

explanation.surface: A single run scored, but none at the opening, by the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a single is one run; 'not opening' drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a hearth or chimney corner.

clue.text: Majestic note struck for treat like this

parts.note: regal means royal or majestic
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A grand musical note played to entertain someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain or feast them lavishly.

clue.text: Drink to prince on the shelf

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A toast raised to a royal who has been left on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge someone is an old phrase for toasting their health.

clue.text: Fast in old prison

definitions.meaning: a notorious London debtors' prison closed in the nineteenth century

explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift of foot, and the Fleet was a historic London jail for debtors.

clue.text: Volcanic material for example coming up for washing

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters rise, read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Volcanic rock rising up to be cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns EG into GE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavage is the medical term for rinsing out a body cavity, a type of cleansing.

clue.text: Glossy coat of celebrity held by the Spanish

indicators.note: held by means the celebrity sits inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
a name is a famous person, as in 'a big name'

explanation.surface: A Spanish star wearing a shiny jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' suggests clothing, but the definition is a shiny finish; 'held by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard shiny paint or glaze, a gleaming coating.

clue.text: Much criticized, deeply offended

definitions.meaning: severely attacked by critics, as a reviewed play may be

explanation.definitionFit: A savaged book is said to be slated in this way, and someone badly hurt is described with the same phrase.

clue.text: Ungodly prospector's vessel has silver in it

indicators.note: in it places the silver within the prospector's dish

parts.note: gold prospectors wash gravel in a pan
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A gold prospector's pan turns up silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold prospectors swirl gravel in a shallow dish; 'in it' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is a heathen, not following a mainstream religion, hence ungodly.

clue.text: Weak food for Rabelais's buffoon in the second half

indicators.note: in the second half means only the latter part of the name is kept

parts.note: Pantagruel is the comic giant of Rabelais's satire

explanation.surface: Thin fare served to a comic character late in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantagruel is the giant hero of Rabelais's sixteenth-century comic novels; keep its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is a thin watery porridge, a feeble meal.

clue.text: But Open University students can not be punished so

definitions.text: But Open University students can not be punished so

parts.words: But Open University students can not be punished so
parts.note: students confined to college as a punishment cannot be so treated when they study at a distance with no campus

explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is a British distance-learning university with no residential campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined to college grounds is a traditional university punishment, impossible for remote learners.

clue.text: How, for example, to make nast retsina?

definitions.text: How, for example, to make nast retsina?

parts.words: How, for example, to make nast retsina?
parts.note: the nonsense phrase is a jumbled version of other letters, so it describes the act of jumbling

explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange letters to form a new phrase is exactly what turns words into nonsense like this.

clue.text: Led in true variety entracte

indicators.note: variety suggests a varied mix, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Led into a true variety show interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' signals an anagram of LED IN TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is a break or musical piece between acts of a play, also called an intermission.
